Today's macOS Tahoe 26.7 candidate release contains a short video clip that appears to demonstrate the operation of Apple's rumored camera-equipped AirPods. Please watch the following segment.

macOS 26.7 includes a demonstration of camera-equipped AirPods

MacRumors discovered a short video clip in today's macOS Tahoe 26.7 RC, in which a man wearing AirPods appears to ask Siri to remember the book he is reading. The Siri voiceover reads as follows:

The camera itself is not visible in the clip, and the earphones look very similar to the current AirPods Pro. The most obvious difference is the stem section, which appears to be slightly thicker.

Aaron Perris has also posted the same clip on X:

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman previously reported that Apple may launch camera-equipped AirPods as early as this year, with the internal codename B790. Earlier, MacRumors also found references to B790 in the macOS 26.7 RC, including code for "image stream".

Interestingly, this batch of AirPods is reportedly separate from another camera-equipped model that Bloomberg said Apple has been developing with the internal codename B798, which is not expected to launch until 2027.

Given that Apple decided to hide this demonstration clip within the macOS 26.7 RC, these camera-equipped AirPods are very likely to be officially announced at next month's iPhone launch event.

What are your thoughts on this clip? Feel free to share them in the comments section.
